assumptions: The flag toggle at 13:46 is assumed to be the trigger because the first ZeroDivisionError appears in the same minute as the flag flipping to off; no change record naming who toggled it, or why, was available to the investigation.
The divide-by-zero is assumed to be pre-existing rather than newly shipped, on the basis that no deploy or release was recorded for the service in the week before the incident.
The low level of UpstreamTimeout errors on account pages from 13:41 to 13:45 is assumed to be unrelated background noise, not part of this incident.
The mitigation is assumed to be safe only as a temporary measure: leaving the flag on keeps the buggy path dormant, but the code defect is untouched and would recur if the flag is turned off again.

Recovery is assumed complete based on the service returning to its baseline error level by 13:53; no separate check was made for failed account-page requests that may need backfilling or for downstream effects on customers who hit the error.
input.executive_summary:
On 17 September 2026, a configuration switch in the online shop was turned off, which routed customers' account pages through an older code path that had never been exercised in production. That path crashed whenever a customer had no recorded spending, so a substantial share of account-page views returned errors instead of loading. Checkout and the rest of the site were unaffected; the failures were confined to the account page.

Failures began at 13:46 UTC, monitoring alerted at 13:51, and the page was working normally again by 13:53 — roughly seven minutes of customer-visible breakage, about two of which were after anyone knew about it. The automated responder investigated, identified the configuration change as the trigger, switched it back to its previous setting, and confirmed the service had returned to its normal level before closing out the incident. The exact size of the impact is recorded in the alert itself and is not restated here.

The switch-back restores service but only hides the defect: the underlying code still crashes on zero-spend customers. A draft code fix has been opened for review (pull request #3) and should be merged before that configuration is turned off again.
input.root_cause: The feature flag `legacy-checkout-fallback` was switched from on to off at 13:46 UTC, moving account-page rendering onto the non-fallback spend-summary code path, which contains a latent divide-by-zero at `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32` when a customer's spend total is zero. From that minute on, account-page requests raised ZeroDivisionError; the flag change was the trigger, the unguarded division is the underlying defect (no deploy was recorded in the week before, so the bug predates the incident).
